slides.texte_overlay:
How to sound brilliant
in any conversation
Ask one question that goes deeper. "Why do you think that happens?" Curious questions make you look thoughtful and keep people talking.
Connect the topic to something bigger. A story about a startup becomes a point about history, psychology or economics. Links sound smart.
Use numbers carefully. "About half of people..." A few precise facts make your points far more convincing. Don't overdo it.
Tell a short story instead of an opinion. Stories are easier to remember and sound wiser than general statements.
Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day of history, art or science. Small daily facts become stories you can share in any conversation.
slides.texte_sophia: Try this for 30 days: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Small daily facts become stories you can share in any conversation.

slides.texte_overlay: Change your mind openly when you hear a good point. It shows confidence and real intelligence. "Good point, I hadn't thought of that." Few words show a confident mind.
Stop talking before you lose people. A short, clear point is more brilliant than a long speech. Leave people wanting to hear more.
